extracted.intended_audience: people planning to compete in the O. Henry Museum Pun-Off World Championships (performers/contestants)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluation criteria for entering and performing in the Pun-Off World Championships, covering both the Punniest of Show routine event and the head-to-head PunSlingers format, plus registration, timing, and adjudication procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event entry & lottery limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A maximum of thirty-two (32) entrants per event will be accepted in a random lottery. Contestants may enter either or both contests (Punniest of Show and PunSlingers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Online registration opens for a limited window (example: noon CDT March 1 to 11:59 pm CDT March 4). A lottery will determine entrants; registration is required for each event separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-site sign-in and packet pickup
rubrics_metrics.description: Contestants selected by lottery must sign in and pick up their registration packet at the Pun-Off location between 10:00 am - 10:45 am on the day of the Pun-Off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Packets not picked up may be assigned to other names on the stand-by waiting list. Contestants unable to meet these requirements must contact organizers to make other arrangements ASAP or the day before the competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punniest of Show routine length allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Each contestant will be allowed to present a routine lasting up to two minutes. Contestants should endeavor to keep their routines ninety (90) seconds in length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timekeeper allows for audience response and technical difficulties; at 90 seconds a warning signal sounds and a 30-second grace period begins; at two minutes a second signal sounds and contestant will be asked to leave the stage. Exceeding 2 minutes results in automatic disqualification. Emcee(s) make final determination of elapsed time; Masters of Ceremonies may adjust time if an incorrect/inadvertent signal occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punniest of Show permitted formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Contestants may use any format (e.g., visual, musical, stand-up routine, shaggy dog, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contestants may use notes or scripts but should keep in mind that the judges may consider this when determining their score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punniest of Show scoring scale and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Routines will be scored on a scale of 1 to 100 by a panel of judges. A contestant's score will be determined after eliminating the highest and lowest scores and totaling the remaining scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a judge displays a score greater than 100 or less than 1, that score will be lowered or raised to the nearest allowable score (e.g., 110 becomes 100, 0 becomes 1). The contestant with the highest score is declared the winner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punniest judging criteria (content, originality, general effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contestants may be judged on content, originality, and general effect of the presentation, including judges' interpretation of audience response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges explicitly may take audience reaction into account as part of general effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punniest tie-break procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of a tie score, the tied contestants will be called back on stage, where they will present part of their routine again; after all tied contestants finish, the audience response will be taken to determine the winner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The contestant that receives the best audience reaction, as determined by the judging panel and the Master(s) of Ceremonies, shall win the event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic disqualification for exceeding time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Any contestant whose presentation exceeds 2 minutes is automatically disqualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although judges may still give a score for the routine, exceeding the two-minute maximum disqualifies the contestant. Emcee(s) will make the final determination based on timekeeper signals; Masters may adjust for incorrect signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: PunSlingers match format and progression
rubrics_metrics.description: PunSlingers consists of five rounds of single-elimination heats. For each preliminary round, two contestants are paired, given a topic, and alternate delivering puns; the survivor of each pairing advances to the next round until a champion is declared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There will be a ten-minute time limit in any bout. In the event of an odd number of contestants, a round may consist of three contestants with two being eliminated. The survivor of the final bout is declared champion PUNSLINGER.

rubrics_metrics.name: PunSlingers delivery time ('five beats')
rubrics_metrics.description: The contestant with the lower entry number has 5 beats to deliver a pun on the topic; the other contestant then has a five count to respond with another pun on the topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contestants who exceed the allotted five count will be eliminated from the competition. Timekeeping (beat counting) by emcees will allow for audience response and technical difficulties; emcee(s) make final determination. In event of incorrect/inadvertent bell signal, Masters may adjust remaining time.

rubrics_metrics.name: PunSlingers word-reuse prohibition and strikes
rubrics_metrics.description: Puns may NOT be made on the same word during a round. A contestant who violates this rule will receive a 'strike' and be given another five count to come up with a pun that has not been used during the pairing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three 'strikes' against either contestant immediately end the round. In the first round of 32, at the discretion of the emcee, an acceptable 'repair' may be offered; an unsatisfactory 'repair' will be considered a strike. After the PunSlingers first round, emcees will not give any do-overs for a 'repaired' pun and a strike will be awarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: PunSlingers judging and winner selection
rubrics_metrics.description: A panel of judges will pick a winner of each round (in addition to time/strike rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges pick winners for rounds; emcee may change, define, or narrow the topic or draw a new topic before starting any round. Time limits and strikes also determine elimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contestant numbering and order of appearance
rubrics_metrics.description: During registration, contestants receive a number for each event entered; these numbers determine order of appearance and pairings. Contestants will not be allowed to trade or exchange numbers unless cleared by emcee(s) or registration officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punniest of Show contestants appear in numerical order starting at 1 and ending at 32; if fewer than 32 enter, non-selected entry numbers are skipped. PunSlingers pairings follow drawn numbers; if max of 32 not reached, contestants paired against numerically closest entry. If a contestant leaves before their number is drawn or does not respond when called, their number is skipped and they are disqualified for that event for the day. If odd number in first round, an unpaired contestant receives a bye to the next round.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master(s) of Ceremonies final authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The Master(s) of Ceremonies shall have final authority over all phases of registration and both contests, including interpretation and implementation of these rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They shall not overrule or change positions determined by judges' scores in Punniest of Show except in matters of an exceeded time limit and/or audience response, but otherwise have final say.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timekeeper signal protocol and adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: The timekeeper will sound a warning at 90 seconds, indicating a 30-second grace period; at the end of two minutes a second signal will be sounded and the contestant asked to leave the stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timekeeper will allow for audience response and technical difficulties when determining if counts have passed. In the event of an incorrect or inadvertent signal from the timekeeper/bell ringer, the Master(s) of Ceremonies will, as they deem necessary, adjust the contestant's remaining time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score correction for out-of-range judge marks
rubrics_metrics.description: If a judge displays a score greater than 100 or less than 1, that score will be lowered or raised to the nearest allowable score (i.e., a 110 becomes a 100, a 0 becomes a 1, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures all judge scores fall within the 1–100 range before high/low elimination and totaling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation of liability / responsibility clause
rubrics_metrics.description: No employee of the O. Henry Museum or the City of Austin, nor any member of, or anyone officially associated with the Brush Square Museums Foundation, emcee, or judge shall be held liable in any way for the final outcome of either contest or for any other matter regarding the competition as a whole or in part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit non-liability statement covering organizers, emcees, judges, and affiliated organizations.
